plan_a_advantages: Increased focus on long, steady-state runs for trail endurance.
Incorporation of hill sessions to build climbing strength.
More consistent aerobic base building through longer easy runs.
plan_b_advantages: Includes dedicated speed work (intervals) for improving pace.
Incorporates strength training to support trail running efforts.
Cross-training to maintain overall fitness outside of trail running.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it prioritizes building a strong aerobic base and trail-specific endurance through extended, easy-paced runs. While Plan B includes valuable speed work, it lacks the consistent volume of long, steady runs crucial for trail running, which demands significant leg strength and cardiovascular capacity. Plan A’s focus on longer durations at a controlled effort will better translate to the demands of a trail race, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on intervals could lead to burnout or insufficient adaptation for the sustained effort required on technical trails. Furthermore, the inclusion of dedicated hill sessions in Plan A directly addresses a key element of trail running performance.
